extracted.intended_audience: authors submitting manuscripts to Wiley journals
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and submitting an authors' contribution statement using the CRediT (Contributor Roles Taxonomy), including required roles, responsibility for accuracy, and publication of the statement with the final article.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to provide CRediT information
rubrics_metrics.description: Journals mandating CRediT (Contributor Roles Taxonomy) will enable authors to provide information on submission, allowing for detailed information about individual contributions to the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not provided on submission, this information can be provided at subsequent revision stages, facilitated by the Editorial Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submitting author responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The submitting author is responsible for ensuring that contributions of all authors are correct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is expected that all authors will have reviewed, discussed and agreed to their individual contributions as shared by the submitting author.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of authors' contribution statement
rubrics_metrics.description: The authors’ contribution statement will be published with the final article and should accurately reflect contributions to the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure accuracy because the statement becomes public and may be referenced if questions about authorship arise after publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistent capture of roles for single- and multi-author papers
rubrics_metrics.description: For consistency, it is important to capture the roles played by a single author on a single-authored paper in the same way as for multi-author papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This facilitates readers’ understanding of an author’s expertise and can also be helpful should any questions arise regarding authorship after publication. A single author does not have to fulfil all the CRediT roles—only those which are relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of degree/level of contribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may indicate degree of contribution (e.g., lead, supporting, equal) alongside role names in the contribution statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example provided shows authors with roles annotated as 'lead', 'supporting', or 'equal' (e.g., 'Conceptualization (lead); writing – original draft (lead); ... review and editing (equal)'). Use such qualifiers to clarify relative contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conceptualization
rubrics_metrics.description: Ideas; formulation or evolution of overarching research goals and aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data Curation
rubrics_metrics.description: Management activities to annotate (produce metadata), scrub data and maintain research data (including software code, where it is necessary for interpreting the data itself) for initial use and later reuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal Analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Application of statistical, mathematical, computational, or other formal techniques to analyze or synthesize study data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding Acquisition
rubrics_metrics.description: Acquisition of the financial support for the project leading to this publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Conducting a research and investigation process, specifically performing the experiments, or data/evidence collection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Development or design of methodology; creation of models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Administration
rubrics_metrics.description: Management and coordination responsibility for the research activity planning and execution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Provision of study materials, reagents, materials, patients, laboratory samples, animals, instrumentation, computing resources, or other analysis tools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Software
rubrics_metrics.description: Programming, software development; designing computer programs; implementation of the computer code and supporting algorithms; testing of existing code components.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supervision
rubrics_metrics.description: Oversight and leadership responsibility for the research activity planning and execution, including mentorship external to the core team.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validation
rubrics_metrics.description: Verification, whether as a part of the activity or separate, of the overall replication/reproducibility of results/experiments and other research outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visualization
rubrics_metrics.description: Preparation, creation and/or presentation of the published work, specifically visualization/data presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing – Original Draft Preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: Creation and/or presentation of the published work, specifically writing the initial draft (including substantive translation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing – Review & Editing
rubrics_metrics.description: Preparation, creation and/or presentation of the published work by those from the original research group, specifically critical review, commentary or revision – including pre- or post-publication stages.
